Aug. 16Trump had a 35% approval rating and 55% disapproval rating in a Financial Times/Focaldata poll of 1,913 registered voters conducted Aug. 7-10 (margin of error 2.9).

Trump’s net approval rating among Republicans has dropped eight points since the groups’ survey last month, the Financial Times reported.

The poll comes as inflation cooled in July from June, but at 3.4%, it’s still higher than when Trump took office as the war with Iran has driven up fuel costs and disrupted the economy. PEW RESEARCH CENTER

Trump’s approval rating over the course of his second term so far has averaged 84% among Republicans and 6% among Democrats – a 78 percentage point gap. This is nearly identical to the 80-point gap over the course of Trump’s first term. (Note: These ratings are among Republicans and Democrats only. They exclude independents who lean toward each party to allow for comparisons to past presidencies.)
